hero.title: Tolkien's Middle-earth
hero.lede: From the Music that made the world to the departure of the Ring-bearers. The map shows where everything happens, the ruler of the Ages shows when, and the profiles explain the peoples, the languages and the people. Tap any underlined name to open its profile.
map.title: The map
map.intro: The west of Middle-earth at the end of the Third Age, drawn in the manner of old maps. Tap a point to read about the place. The lands that no longer exist at that time are listed below the map.
map.lost: Lands of ancient ages, off this map
map.cartSubtitle: the West, at the end of the Third Age
eras.title: The Ages
eras.intro: The width of each band follows the length of the Age in Sun years. The First Age, the most often told, is the shortest of the three.
explore.title: Peoples, languages and characters
explore.intro: Each profile carries its links to other profiles and the moments of the timeline in which it appears. The profiles reveal how the stories end.
books.title: The books
books.intro: Where each part of the story is told. Titles and dates of the original editions.
books.startP1: Publication order works best: The Hobbit, The Lord of the Rings with the Appendices, and only then The Silmarillion. It is denser and gains a great deal once the reader already knows the Third Age.
books.startP2: After The Silmarillion, the three great tales of the First Age (The Children of Húrin, Beren and Lúthien, The Fall of Gondolin) deepen what it summarizes, and Unfinished Tales and The Fall of Númenor cover the Second Age.

credits.label: Sources and credits
credits.sourcesText: The foundation is the books of J.R.R. Tolkien, above all the Appendices of The Lord of the Rings and The Silmarillion. Dates and names were checked against Tolkien Gateway and Wikipedia.
credits.namesText: Names follow Tolkien's original English editions (Dwarves, Orcs, Mirkwood). Readers of the Brazilian HarperCollins translation may know other forms, such as Anãos, Orques and Trevamata.
credits.mapTitle: About the map and the dates
credits.mapText: The map is an original drawing, in the manner of old maps, without an exact scale. Dates before the Sun come from the annals that Tolkien left in draft and vary between versions.
